question.:question/problem:

Consider the picture above. If $c=\lambda a+b,$ then$\,\lambda =$
{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\lambda a+b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $b.$ So, we first draw the vector $b$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186235285/assets/5f8dee860607da2fda18caf8-solution.png)

Let $P$ be the endpoint of the vector $b.$ Then

$$
c=\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC}.
$$

In $△OPC,$ we have:

- $PC=4|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{PC}$ and $a$ have opposite directions

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PC}=-4a.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC} \\  & =b-4a.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a+b=-4a+b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $a,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =-4
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\lambda a+2b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $2b.$ So, we first draw the vector $2b$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186235285/assets/ef8d1d96f28cb905ef8f2e5c-solution.png)

Let $P$ be the endpoint of the vector $2b.$ Then

$$
c=\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC}.
$$

In $△OPC,$ we have:

- $PC=4|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{PC}$ and $a$ have opposite directions

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PC}=-4a.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC} \\  & =2b-4a.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a+2b=-4a+2b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $a,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =-4
$$
